run.notes: FIRST SERVE ON THIS RIG. Until this run gpu-jax-g4dn-2b had provisioned nothing and measured nothing, and both server.py and README.md carried the G5g sibling's numbers relabelled as this rig's own. Spot i-02eb43cb99429a8f7 in us-east-1b, launched, deployed, measured and terminated in one cycle. Driven end to end by tune_loop.py, so the served build id was asserted equal to the local payload digest (51bc52c9e2e9) before any number was recorded.

model.architecture_notes: 28 sliding layers at head_dim=256, 7 full-attention at global_head_dim=512; 8 query heads to 1 KV head (full MQA). KV sharing from layer 15 collapses to two source caches (13 sliding, 14 full), so 15 caches exist, not 35, and window_kv=True caps the 12 sliding ones at the 512-slot ring. Whole KV cache at 4K is ~30 MiB — KV is not the binding constraint here, prefill is.

software.backend: cuda (jax[cuda13], pip-supplied CUDA; DLAMI supplies only the driver)

workload.notes: Median of 3, warmed AT THE SHAPE MEASURED — max_new_tokens is a static_argnames entry, so (bucket, max_tokens) is the compiled shape and warming at a different max_tokens has previously been a 4x error. per_stream_tok_per_s is the server's own tpu_jax_decode_tokens_per_second gauge; output_tok_per_s is end-to-end wall including prefill and HTTP, which is why it falls with context while the gauge does not.

sweep.error: MAX_NUM_SEQS=1: Gemma4EModelJAX raises NotImplementedError for B > 1, and the decode step donates its KV buffers. Batching is closed by the engine, not by capacity.

memory.notes: tpu_jax_weight_bytes 6.155 GB, tpu_jax_hbm_used_bytes 6.197 GB. The T4 reports 15360 MiB via nvidia-smi — IDENTICAL to the T4G, and NOT the 16384 MiB that describe_instance_types implies. README.md predicted a real 1 GiB advantage here on that basis; the device disagrees, and the device is what allocates.

startup.notes: Instance RUNNING 19:01:26Z, service start 19:04:10Z, READY 19:06:41Z. Cloud-init install was 76s TOTAL including xprof and tensorboard: apt-base 6s, python-3.14 1s (already the system interpreter on the Ubuntu 26.04 base, so deadsnakes was skipped), pip-bootstrap 6s, jax-wheels 42s, serving-deps 13s, profiling-deps 5s, gpu-verify 3s. No compilation cache was restored — JAX_CACHE_S3_URI is empty by default.

cost.notes: rate_per_chip_hour is the SPOT rate actually paid, $0.3724/hr in us-east-1b, and g4dn.xlarge carries exactly one T4 so instance rate and per-chip rate coincide. On-demand list is $0.526/hr. The whole launch-to-terminate cycle was about 25 minutes, so roughly $0.16. Spot capacity was NOT available in us-east-1a (InsufficientInstanceCapacity) and 1a was not the cheapest AZ, so price remains a bad proxy for capacity — retry across AZs.

issues.summary: tune_loop.py hardcoded the <hw-short> suffix as 'g5g', so this rig's first run landed in benchmarks/runs/2026-08-29-first-serve-g5g — a directory name asserting hardware the run did not happen on.
issues.resolution: HW_SHORT now derives from slot 3 of the rig directory name.

issues.summary: The instance role's S3 policy enumerated per-rig prefixes (gpu-jax-g5g-2b, gpu-jax-g6-2b) and so denied this rig's artifact upload, which tune_loop.py depends on. Every fork needed an IAM edit before it could return a measurement.
issues.resolution: jax-compilation-cache-rw was LOOSENED rather than extended: the rig segment is now a wildcard, so the grant is vllm-models-bucket/{jax-cache,benchmarks}/* for any rig. Deliberate operator decision — a new rig should not need an IAM change to write its own cache and results. Still scoped to those two prefixes inside the one bucket; the bucket boundary did not move.

notes: THE A/B LANDED ON TOP OF THE SIBLING. This rig exists to separate Turing from Graviton2: same engine, same checkpoint, same dtype policy, same SM 7.5, different host ISA. Decode 13.1/13.2/13.1 tok/s against gpu-jax-g5g-2b's 13.10 at the identical ple4+int8head config, and tpu_jax_weight_bytes 6.155 GB against 6.155 GB — exact.

The xprof profile reproduces the sibling's to within noise: dtype conversion 54.4% (g5g 54.4 / 54.0), fp32 GEMV 32.8% (32.6 / 32.8), TensorCore 0.0% (0.0). Roofline peaks are IDENTICAL to three decimals — peak FLOP 65126.4, peak HBM 298.083 GiB/s, ridge 203.479.

CONCLUSION: the host architecture contributes nothing measurable to decode, and the 86.9% dtype-plus-fp32-GEMV tax is purely a Turing property. gpu-jax-g5g-2b's finding is therefore a chip finding, not a Graviton2 one, and its falsification of the weight-dtype fix (2026-08-28: a GEMV has no half path at B=1) carries here unchanged. The route to the ceiling is a GEMM — batching — which MAX_NUM_SEQS=1 closes.

What the host DID change is packaging risk, and it should not be quoted as a finding: on x86_64 the wheel-availability argument that mattered on aarch64 is nearly vacuous. The load-bearing claim was always sm_75.

xprof 2.23.1 and tensorboard 2.21.0 are now installed AT BOOT as their own non-fatal stage, 5 seconds of a 76-second install. They were previously on-demand via a documented path inside APP_DIR that the deploy payload excludes, so they were in practice never installed at all.
